title: The School of Athens
caption:
Every genius in one room. Can you name them?

Raphael painted The School of Athens on a wall in the Vatican in 1509–11, and filled it with thinkers who lived centuries apart. Plato and Aristotle argue at the centre. Diogenes sprawls on the steps. Pythagoras and Euclid work out the numbers. And one young man in a black cap is looking straight back at you.

Swipe for all eight, then find them on the map at the end.

Which one would you want to meet?

slides.headline: Every genius in one room.
slides.alt: The vaulted hall of the School of Athens with the crowd of philosophers small on the steps below.

slides.headline: One points up. One points down.
slides.alt: Plato pointing upward with his Timaeus beside Aristotle holding his palm over the ground, Ethics under his arm. Numbered 01 of 08.

slides.headline: The man who rejected everything.
slides.alt: Diogenes sprawled alone across the marble steps in a blue robe, reading a sheet. Numbered 02.

slides.headline: The man who heard the numbers.
slides.alt: Pythagoras writing in a book on his knee while a boy holds a slate of musical ratios. Numbered 03.

slides.headline: The man drawing on the floor.
slides.alt: Euclid, bald, bending over a slate with a compass as students crowd round. Numbered 04.

slides.headline: The loneliest man in the room.
slides.alt: Heraclitus sitting alone against a marble block, chin on his fist, writing. Numbered 05.

slides.headline: Two men holding the world.
slides.alt: Bearded Zoroaster holding a starry sphere and crowned Ptolemy, seen from behind, holding a globe of the Earth. Numbered 06.

slides.headline: The man who questioned everything.
slides.alt: Socrates in an olive robe counting on his fingers to a young listener. Numbered 07.

slides.headline: The painter hid himself inside.
slides.alt: Raphael in a black cap at the far right, looking out at the viewer beside an older man in a white cap. Numbered 08.

slides.headline: One wall. A world of ideas.
slides.alt: The whole fresco in a gold frame with eight numbered gold discs on the figures, and a key listing their names.

notes: Who's-who style (new, 21 Nov 2026): one numbered figure per slide, full-bleed crops from the 17402 px Commons scan, numeral in the text block so it never covers a face, then a map numbering all eight. Slide 2 (Plato & Aristotle) doubles as the second hook. Old story version: archive/slides-story-v1.html (its images in img/archive/). Identifications are traditional; Euclid/Bramante and Heraclitus/Michelangelo hedged ('said to be', 'widely read as'); Zoroaster/Ptolemy hedged 'traditionally'. Raphael's self-portrait stated by the Vatican Museums. Map discs placed by eye on each figure's head.
